connections.label: David calls him Lord
connections.explanation: Mark 12:35–37 quotes Psalms 110:1: teaching in the temple, Jesus asks how the scribes can call the Christ David's son when David, by the Holy Spirit, calls him Lord. The psalm has the LORD tell David's lord to sit at his right hand until his enemies are his footstool. The crowd hears him gladly.

ends.excerpt: The LORD says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.”

ends.sectionTitle: Entry into Jerusalem; Questions in the Temple
ends.excerpt: Jesus responded, as he taught in the temple, “How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?

connections.label: A priest after the order of Melchizedek
connections.explanation: Hebrews 7:15–17 quotes Psalms 110:4: Hebrews rests its case for Christ's priesthood on the oath that he is a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek. The psalm makes the king a priest by God's sworn word; Hebrews argues that such a priest rises by the power of an endless life, not by descent from Levi.

ends.excerpt: The LORD has sworn, and will not change his mind: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
This is yet more abundantly evident, if after the likeness of Melchizedek there arises another priest,

connections.label: You are my Son
connections.explanation: Hebrews 1:5 quotes Psalms 2:7: to show the Son greater than the angels, Hebrews asks to which of them God ever said, you are my Son, today I have become your father. In the psalm the LORD says it to his anointed king on Zion.

ends.excerpt: I will tell of the decree: The LORD said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.

ends.sectionTitle: The Son above the Angels and Moses; the Promised Rest
ends.excerpt: For to which of the angels did he say at any time, “You are my Son. Today I have become your father?” and again, “I will be to him a Father, and he will be to me a Son?”

connections.label: What is man, that you think of him?
connections.explanation: Hebrews 2:6–8 quotes Psalms 8:4–6: the psalm's wonder that God made man a little lower than the angels and put all things under his feet. Hebrews notes that we do not yet see all things subject to man, but we see Jesus, made lower for a little while and now crowned with glory.

ends.excerpt: what is man, that you think of him? What is the son of man, that you care for him? For you have made him a little lower than the angels, and crowned him with glory and honor.

ends.sectionTitle: The Son above the Angels and Moses; the Promised Rest
ends.excerpt: But one has somewhere testified, saying, “What is man, that you think of him? Or the son of man, that you care for him?

connections.label: Today, if you hear his voice
connections.explanation: Hebrews 3:7–11 quotes Psalms 95:7–11: Hebrews gives the psalm's warning as the Holy Spirit's word, not to harden hearts as in the wilderness. There the fathers tested God for forty years, and he swore they would not enter his rest. Hebrews goes on to argue that a rest remains for God's people.

ends.excerpt: for he is our God. We are the people of his pasture, and the sheep in his care. Today, oh that you would hear his voice!

ends.excerpt: Therefore, even as the Holy Spirit says, “Today if you will hear his voice, don’t harden your hearts as in the rebellion, in the day of the trial in the wilderness,

connections.label: My God, why have you forsaken me?
connections.explanation: Mark 15:34 quotes Psalms 22:1: at the ninth hour Jesus cries out in Aramaic the opening of the psalm, and Mark gives its meaning. The psalm goes on from abandonment and mockery to praise among the congregation. Some who stand by mishear it as a call to Elijah.

ends.excerpt: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, and from the words of my groaning?
At the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?” which is, being interpreted, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”

connections.label: The stone the builders rejected
connections.explanation: Mark 12:10–11 quotes Psalms 118:22–23: Jesus ends the parable of the wicked tenants with the psalm's rejected stone that became the head of the corner. The psalm calls it the LORD's doing, marvellous in our eyes. The priests and scribes see that he told the parable against them.

ends.excerpt: The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is the LORD’s doing. It is marvelous in our eyes.

ends.sectionTitle: Entry into Jerusalem; Questions in the Temple
ends.excerpt: Haven’t you even read this Scripture: ‘The stone which the builders rejected was made the head of the corner.

connections.label: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord
connections.explanation: Mark 11:9 quotes Psalms 118:26: the crowds going before and after Jesus into Jerusalem cry Hosanna and the psalm's blessing on the one who comes in the LORD's name. In the psalm it greets the one entering the temple gates in procession.

ends.excerpt: Blessed is he who comes in the LORD’s name! We have blessed you out of the LORD’s house. The LORD is God, and he has given us light. Bind the sacrifice with cords, even to the horns of the altar.

ends.sectionTitle: Entry into Jerusalem; Questions in the Temple
ends.excerpt: Those who went in front and those who followed cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!

connections.label: A body you prepared for me
connections.explanation: Hebrews 10:5–7 quotes Psalms 40:6–8: Hebrews puts the psalm in Christ's mouth as he comes into the world: sacrifices and offerings God did not desire, and the speaker comes to do God's will. Hebrews follows the Greek, a body prepared, where the Hebrew speaks of ears opened.

ends.excerpt: Sacrifice and offering you didn’t desire. You have opened my ears. You have not required burnt offering and sin offering.

ends.sectionTitle: The New Covenant and the Once-for-All Sacrifice
ends.excerpt: Therefore when he comes into the world, he says, “You didn’t desire sacrifice and offering, but you prepared a body for me.

connections.label: Whoever would love life
connections.explanation: 1 Peter 3:10–12 quotes Psalms 34:12–16: First Peter grounds its call not to repay evil for evil in the psalm. Whoever wants good days must keep his tongue from evil, turn from evil, and seek peace and pursue it, for the Lord's eyes are on the righteous.

ends.excerpt: Who is someone who desires life, and loves many days, that he may see good? Keep your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking lies.

ends.sectionTitle: Suffering for Doing Good; Shepherds of the Flock
ends.excerpt: For, “He who would love life and see good days, let him keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit.

connections.label: None righteous, no, not one
connections.explanation: Romans 3:10–12 quotes Psalms 14:1–3: Paul opens his chain of Scriptures on universal sin with the psalm's verdict that there is none who does good, not even one; all have turned aside together. In the psalm it is God's view of the earth from heaven, where the fool says there is no God.

ends.excerpt: The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt. They have done abominable deeds. There is no one who does good.

ends.sectionTitle: The Gospel; All under Sin; Righteousness through Faith
ends.excerpt: As it is written, “There is no one righteous; no, not one. There is no one who understands. There is no one who seeks after God.

connections.label: Blessed is he whose sin is forgiven
connections.explanation: Romans 4:7–8 quotes Psalms 32:1–2: Paul cites David's blessing on those whose sins are covered and to whom the LORD does not count iniquity, as a picture of righteousness counted apart from works. The psalm goes on to tell of the relief of confessing.

ends.excerpt: Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man to whom the LORD doesn’t impute iniquity, in whose spirit there is no deceit.

ends.sectionTitle: Abraham’s Faith; Peace with God; Adam and Christ
ends.excerpt: “Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man whom the Lord will by no means charge with sin.”

connections.label: The reproaches of those who reproached you
connections.explanation: Romans 15:3 quotes Psalms 69:9: Paul urges the strong to bear with the weak because Christ did not please himself, but as written, the reproaches of those who reproached God fell on him. The psalm says it of one consumed by zeal for God's house.

ends.excerpt: For the zeal of your house consumes me. The reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen on me.

ends.sectionTitle: The Weak and the Strong; Paul’s Plans and Greetings
ends.excerpt: For even Christ didn’t please himself. But, as it is written, “The reproaches of those who reproached you fell on me.”

connections.label: I believed, therefore I spoke
connections.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:13 quotes Psalms 116:10: Paul claims the psalmist's spirit of faith, I believed and therefore I spoke, for his own preaching in the face of death. The psalm is thanks for rescue from the cords of death.

ends.excerpt: I believed, therefore I said, “I was greatly afflicted.” I said in my haste, “All people are liars.”

ends.sectionTitle: Ministers of the New Covenant; Reconciliation
ends.excerpt: But having the same spirit of faith, according to that which is written, “I believed, and therefore I spoke.” We also believe, and therefore we also speak,

connections.label: He ascended on high
connections.explanation: Ephesians 4:8 quotes Psalms 68:18: Ephesians reads the psalm of God going up on high and leading captives as Christ's ascension, adding that he gave gifts to men. The Hebrew psalm speaks of receiving gifts among men; Ephesians draws from it the gifts of apostles, prophets, evangelists, shepherds and teachers.

ends.excerpt: You have ascended on high. You have led away captives. You have received gifts among people, yes, among the rebellious also, that the LORD God might dwell there.

ends.sectionTitle: Unity and the New Life; the Household; the Armour of God
ends.excerpt: Therefore he says, “When he ascended on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts to people.”

connections.label: A rod of iron
connections.explanation: Revelation 2:26–27 quotes Psalms 2:8–9: the risen Christ promises the one who overcomes in Thyatira authority over the nations, to rule them with a rod of iron. In the psalm God gives the nations to his anointed king, to break them like a potter's vessel.

ends.excerpt: Ask of me, and I will give the nations for your inheritance, the uttermost parts of the earth for your possession.
He who overcomes, and he who keeps my works to the end, to him I will give authority over the nations.

connections.label: I will open my mouth in parables
connections.explanation: Matthew 13:35 quotes Psalms 78:2: Matthew says Jesus spoke to the crowds in parables to fulfil the psalm's I will open my mouth in parables. Matthew names the speaker a prophet; the psalm is Asaph's retelling of Israel's history, things hidden from of old.

ends.excerpt: I will open my mouth in a parable. I will utter dark sayings of old, which we have heard and known, and our fathers have told us.
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying, “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.”

connections.label: Out of the mouths of babies
connections.explanation: Matthew 21:16 quotes Psalms 8:2: when the chief priests object to children crying Hosanna in the temple, Jesus answers with the psalm's praise from the mouths of babies. Matthew follows the Greek, praise, where the Hebrew has strength.

ends.excerpt: From the lips of babes and infants you have established strength, because of your adversaries, that you might silence the enemy and the avenger.

ends.sectionTitle: Entry into Jerusalem; Controversies in the Temple
ends.excerpt: and said to him, “Do you hear what these are saying?” Jesus said to them, “Yes. Did you never read, ‘Out of the mouth of children and nursing babies, you have perfected praise’?”

connections.label: Your throne, O God, is forever
connections.explanation: Hebrews 1:8–9 quotes Psalms 45:6–7: Hebrews takes the royal wedding psalm as God's word to the Son, whose throne is forever and whose sceptre is righteousness. It sets this against what God says of the angels, who are servants.

ends.excerpt: Your throne, God, is forever and ever. A scepter of equity is the scepter of your kingdom.

ends.sectionTitle: The Son above the Angels and Moses; the Promised Rest
ends.excerpt: But of the Son he says, “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever. The scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your Kingdom.

connections.label: They will perish, but you remain
connections.explanation: Hebrews 1:10–12 quotes Psalms 102:25–27: Hebrews gives as said to the Son the psalm's praise of the Lord who laid the earth's foundations. His works wear out like a garment and are changed, but he remains the same and his years have no end.

ends.excerpt: Of old, you laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the work of your hands. They will perish, but you will endure. Yes, all of them will wear out like a garment. You will change them like a…

ends.sectionTitle: The Son above the Angels and Moses; the Promised Rest
ends.excerpt: And, “You, Lord, in the beginning, laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the works of your hands.

connections.label: Their voice has gone out into all the earth
connections.explanation: Romans 10:18 quotes Psalms 19:4: asking whether Israel has not heard, Paul answers with the psalm, whose voice reaches through all the earth and whose words reach the world's ends. The psalm says it of the heavens declaring God's glory; Paul applies it to the preaching of the gospel.

ends.excerpt: Their voice has gone out through all the earth, their words to the end of the world. In them he has set a tent for the sun,

ends.sectionTitle: Israel and the Nations in God’s Plan
ends.excerpt: But I say, didn’t they hear? Yes, most certainly, “Their sound went out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.”

connections.label: Sheep for the slaughter
connections.explanation: Romans 8:36 quotes Psalms 44:22: in naming what cannot part believers from Christ's love, Paul cites the psalm's for your sake we are killed all day long. In the psalm Israel protests that this has come on them though they have not forgotten God.

ends.excerpt: Yes, for your sake we are killed all day long. We are regarded as sheep for the slaughter.
Even as it is written, “For your sake we are killed all day long. We were accounted as sheep for the slaughter.”

connections.label: He will give his angels charge
connections.explanation: Matthew 4:6 quotes Psalms 91:11–12: in the wilderness the devil sets Jesus on the temple's pinnacle and quotes the psalm's promise that angels will bear him up lest he strike his foot against a stone. Jesus answers with Deuteronomy: do not test the Lord your God.

ends.excerpt: For he will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways. They will bear you up in their hands, so that you won’t dash your foot against a stone.

ends.sectionTitle: John the Baptist; the Temptation; the First Disciples
ends.excerpt: and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down, for it is written, ‘He will command his angels concerning you,’ and, ‘On their hands they will bear you up, so that you don’t dash…

connections.label: Depart from me, you who work iniquity
connections.explanation: Matthew 7:23 quotes Psalms 6:8: at the end of the Sermon on the Mount Jesus says he will tell those who called him Lord but did not do the Father's will, depart from me, you who work iniquity. In the psalm the sufferer says it to his enemies when the LORD has heard his weeping.

ends.excerpt: Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity, for the LORD has heard the voice of my weeping.

ends.sectionTitle: The Sermon on the Mount: Prayer and Trust
ends.excerpt: Then I will tell them, ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you who work iniquity.’ “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house…

connections.label: The meek shall inherit the earth
connections.explanation: Matthew 5:5 quotes Psalms 37:11: the third Beatitude blesses the gentle, who will inherit the earth. The psalm promises it to the humble who wait for the LORD and do not fret over evildoers, who will soon be gone.

ends.excerpt: But the humble shall inherit the land, and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.

ends.sectionTitle: The Sermon on the Mount: the Beatitudes and the Law
ends.excerpt: Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth. Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.

connections.label: The earth is the Lord's
connections.explanation: 1 Corinthians 10:26 quotes Psalms 24:1: Paul tells the Corinthians they may eat whatever is sold in the market without asking questions, for the earth is the Lord's and all its fullness. The psalm opens with it before asking who may ascend the LORD's hill.

ends.excerpt: The earth is the LORD’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell in it. For he has founded it on the seas, and established it on the floods.

ends.sectionTitle: Food Offered to Idols; Paul’s Freedom
ends.excerpt: for “the earth is the Lord’s, and its fullness.” But if one of those who don’t believe invites you to a meal, and you are inclined to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for the…

connections.label: Be angry and do not sin
connections.explanation: Ephesians 4:26 quotes Psalms 4:4: Ephesians takes up the psalm's be angry and do not sin, and adds don't let the sun go down on your wrath, nor give the devil a foothold. The psalm goes on to bid the angry search their hearts on their beds and be still.

ends.excerpt: Stand in awe, and don’t sin. Search your own heart on your bed, and be still. Selah. Offer the sacrifices of righteousness. Put your trust in the LORD.

ends.sectionTitle: Unity and the New Life; the Household; the Armour of God
ends.excerpt: “Be angry, and don’t sin.” Don’t let the sun go down on your wrath, and don’t give place to the devil.

connections.label: He has scattered, he has given to the poor
connections.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:9 quotes Psalms 112:9: urging generous giving for the saints in Jerusalem, Paul cites the psalm of the righteous man who has given to the poor. His righteousness endures forever; Paul adds that God supplies seed to the sower.

ends.excerpt: He has dispersed, he has given to the poor. His righteousness endures forever. His horn will be exalted with honor.
As it is written, “He has scattered abroad. He has given to the poor. His righteousness remains forever.”

connections.label: The virgin will conceive
connections.explanation: Matthew 1:22–23 quotes Isaiah 7:14: Matthew says the birth of Jesus fulfilled the word to Ahaz that the virgin will conceive and bear a son, called Immanuel. He translates the name as God with us. Matthew follows the Greek, virgin, where the Hebrew word means a young woman.

ends.sectionTitle: Ahaz, Assyria and the Promised Child
ends.excerpt: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.

connections.explanation: Mark 1:2–3 quotes Isaiah 40:3: Mark opens his Gospel with the voice crying in the wilderness to prepare the Lord's way, under the name of Isaiah. He joins Malachi's messenger sent ahead to it. John the Baptist then appears in the wilderness preaching.

ends.sectionTitle: Comfort for the Exiles; the Servant
ends.excerpt: The voice of one who calls out, “Prepare the way of the LORD in the wilderness! Make a level highway in the desert for our God.

connections.explanation: Matthew 8:17 quotes Isaiah 53:4: after an evening of healing, Matthew says this fulfilled Isaiah: he took our infirmities and bore our diseases. Isaiah says it of the servant who bore the griefs and sorrows of others.

ends.excerpt: Surely he has borne our sickness and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted.

ends.sectionTitle: Healings and the Cost of Following
ends.excerpt: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “He took our infirmities and bore our diseases.”

connections.label: By his wounds you were healed
connections.explanation: 1 Peter 2:22–25 quotes Isaiah 53:4–9: First Peter holds up Christ's suffering to servants in the servant song's words. He did no sin and no deceit was in his mouth; he bore our sins, and by his wounds you were healed. The readers had been going astray like sheep.

ends.excerpt: Surely he has borne our sickness and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted.

ends.excerpt: who didn’t sin, “neither was deceit found in his mouth.” When he was cursed, he didn’t curse back. When he suffered, he didn’t threaten, but committed himself to him who judges righteously.

connections.label: Hearing, they will not understand
connections.explanation: Matthew 13:14–15 quotes Isaiah 6:9–10: Jesus explains why he speaks in parables with the word given at Isaiah's call, that this people will hear and not understand, see and not perceive. Their heart has grown dull. He then blesses the disciples' eyes and ears.

ends.sectionTitle: The Song of the Vineyard; Isaiah’s Call
ends.excerpt: He said, “Go, and tell this people, ‘You hear indeed, but don’t understand. You see indeed, but don’t perceive.’
In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says, ‘By hearing you will hear, and will in no way understand; Seeing you will see, and will in no way perceive;

connections.label: This people honours me with their lips
connections.explanation: Mark 7:6–7 quotes Isaiah 29:13: when Pharisees fault the disciples for unwashed hands, Jesus calls them hypocrites in Isaiah's words. This people honours God with their lips while their heart is far from him, teaching human commands as doctrine.

ends.excerpt: The Lord said, “Because this people draws near with their mouth and honors me with their lips, but they have removed their heart far from me, and their fear of me is a commandment of men which has…

ends.sectionTitle: Clean and Unclean; Four Thousand Fed
ends.excerpt: He answered them, “Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written, ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.

connections.label: My servant whom I have chosen
connections.explanation: Matthew 12:17–21 quotes Isaiah 42:1–4: when Jesus tells those he heals not to make him known, Matthew quotes the servant song at length. God's chosen servant will not quarrel or cry out, nor break a bruised reed, and in his name the Gentiles will hope.

ends.sectionTitle: Comfort for the Exiles; the Servant
ends.excerpt: “Behold, my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights: I have put my Spirit on him. He will bring justice to the nations.
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “Behold, my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved in whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit on him. He…

connections.label: The people who sat in darkness
connections.explanation: Matthew 4:14–16 quotes Isaiah 9:1–2: as Jesus settles in Capernaum, Matthew cites Isaiah's word to Galilee of the nations, that the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light. From then on Jesus begins to preach.

ends.sectionTitle: Ahaz, Assyria and the Promised Child
ends.excerpt: But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious…

ends.sectionTitle: John the Baptist; the Temptation; the First Disciples
ends.excerpt: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, toward the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,

connections.label: A chief cornerstone in Zion
connections.explanation: 1 Peter 2:6 quotes Isaiah 28:16: First Peter calls Christ the living stone and quotes Isaiah's cornerstone laid in Zion, chosen and precious, on which whoever believes will not be put to shame. It goes on to the stone the builders rejected.

ends.excerpt: Therefore the Lord GOD says, “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation. He who believes shall not act hastily.

ends.sectionTitle: New Birth and Hope; a Holy People
ends.excerpt: Because it is contained in Scripture, “Behold, I lay in Zion a chief cornerstone, chosen and precious. He who believes in him will not be disappointed.”

connections.label: A stone of stumbling
connections.explanation: Romans 9:33 quotes Isaiah 8:14: Paul joins two of Isaiah's stones, laying in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence, and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame. He uses it to explain why Israel, pursuing righteousness by works, stumbled.

ends.sectionTitle: Ahaz, Assyria and the Promised Child
ends.excerpt: He will be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel, he will be a stumbling stone and a rock that makes them fall. For the people of Jerusalem, he will be a trap and a snare.

ends.sectionTitle: Israel and the Nations in God’s Plan
ends.excerpt: even as it is written, “Behold, I lay in Zion a stumbling stone and a rock of offense; and no one who believes in him will be disappointed.”

connections.label: How beautiful are the feet
connections.explanation: Romans 10:15 quotes Isaiah 52:7: Paul asks how anyone can preach unless sent, and answers with Isaiah: how beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news. In Isaiah the messenger brings Zion word that her God reigns.

ends.excerpt: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”

ends.sectionTitle: Israel and the Nations in God’s Plan
ends.excerpt: And how will they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the Good News of peace, who bring glad tidings of good things!”

connections.label: The Deliverer will come out of Zion
connections.explanation: Romans 11:26 quotes Isaiah 59:20: Paul ends his argument that all Israel will be saved with Isaiah's promise of a deliverer for Zion who will turn away ungodliness from Jacob. Paul follows the Greek, out of Zion, where the Hebrew has to Zion.

ends.excerpt: “A Redeemer will come to Zion, and to those who turn from disobedience in Jacob,” says the LORD.

ends.sectionTitle: Israel and the Nations in God’s Plan
ends.excerpt: and so all Israel will be saved. Even as it is written, “There will come out of Zion the Deliverer, and he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.

connections.label: Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die
connections.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:32 quotes Isaiah 22:13: Paul argues that if the dead are not raised, the reckless saying might as well be true: let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die. In Isaiah it is Jerusalem's revelry when the LORD called for weeping.

ends.sectionTitle: Against Babylon, Edom, Arabia, Jerusalem and Tyre
ends.excerpt: and behold, there is joy and gladness, killing cattle and killing sheep, eating meat and drinking wine: “Let’s eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die.”
If I fought with animals at Ephesus for human purposes, what does it profit me? If the dead are not raised, then “let’s eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”

connections.label: Death is swallowed up in victory
connections.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:54 quotes Isaiah 25:8: Paul says that when the perishable puts on the imperishable, the saying will come true that death is swallowed up in victory. Isaiah promises it at the LORD's feast on his mountain for all peoples.

ends.sectionTitle: The Earth Judged; a Feast on the Mountain
ends.excerpt: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for the LORD has spoken it.
But when this perishable body will have become imperishable, and this mortal will have put on immortality, then what is written will happen: “Death is swallowed up in victory.”

connections.label: Death, where is your sting?
connections.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:55 quotes Hosea 13:14: straight after Isaiah, Paul taunts death in Hosea's words: death, where is your sting, grave, where is your victory? Hosea asks where death's plagues are; Paul answers that the sting of death is sin, and thanks God for the victory through Christ.

ends.excerpt: I will ransom them from the power of Sheol. I will redeem them from death! Death, where are your plagues? Sheol, where is your destruction? “Compassion will be hidden from my eyes.
“Death, where is your sting? Hades, where is your victory?” The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.

connections.label: No eye has seen
connections.explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:9 quotes Isaiah 64:4: Paul speaks of God's hidden wisdom in words close to Isaiah's: things no eye has seen and no ear heard, which God prepared for those who love him. Isaiah says it of the God who acts for those who wait for him.

ends.excerpt: For from of old men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, nor has the eye seen a God besides you, who works for him who waits for him.

ends.sectionTitle: Divisions and the Wisdom of the Cross
ends.excerpt: But as it is written, “Things which an eye didn’t see, and an ear didn’t hear, which didn’t enter into the heart of man, these God has prepared for those who love him.”

connections.label: Rejoice, barren woman
connections.explanation: Galatians 4:27 quotes Isaiah 54:1: in his figure of Sarah and Hagar, Paul cites Isaiah's call to the barren woman to rejoice, for her children are more than those of the married wife. He reads the Jerusalem above as the free mother of believers.

ends.excerpt: “Sing, barren, you who didn’t give birth! Break out into singing, and cry aloud, you who didn’t travail with child! For more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife,”…

connections.label: Coals of fire on his head
connections.explanation: Romans 12:20 quotes Proverbs 25:21–22: Paul tells believers never to avenge themselves but, as the proverb says, to feed a hungry enemy and give him drink, heaping coals of fire on his head. He ends: overcome evil with good.

ends.excerpt: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink; for you will heap coals of fire on his head, and the LORD will reward you.

ends.sectionTitle: Life in the Body; Love and the Authorities
ends.excerpt: Therefore “If your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him a drink; for in doing so, you will heap coals of fire on his head.”

connections.label: A dog returns to its vomit
connections.explanation: 2 Peter 2:22 quotes Proverbs 26:11: Second Peter says of those who turn back after knowing the way of righteousness that the proverb has come true of them: the dog turns to its own vomit. It adds a second saying about a washed sow.

ends.excerpt: As a dog that returns to his vomit, so is a fool who repeats his folly. Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

ends.sectionTitle: Growing in Grace; False Teachers; the Day of the Lord
ends.excerpt: But it has happened to them according to the true proverb, “The dog turns to his own vomit again,” and “the sow that has washed to wallowing in the mire.”

connections.label: If the righteous is scarcely saved
connections.explanation: 1 Peter 4:18 quotes Proverbs 11:31: First Peter says judgement begins with God's household and asks, with the proverb, what will become of the ungodly if the righteous are scarcely saved. It follows the Greek of the proverb.

ends.sectionTitle: Solomon’s Proverbs: the Righteous and the Wicked
ends.excerpt: Behold, the righteous shall be repaid on the earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!

ends.sectionTitle: Suffering for Doing Good; Shepherds of the Flock
ends.excerpt: “If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will happen to the ungodly and the sinner?”

connections.label: Love covers a multitude of sins
connections.explanation: 1 Peter 4:8 echoes Proverbs 10:12: above all, First Peter says, keep your love for one another fervent, for love covers a multitude of sins. The proverb says that hatred stirs up strife but love covers all wrongs.

ends.sectionTitle: Solomon’s Proverbs: the Righteous and the Wicked
ends.excerpt: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs. Wisdom is found on the lips of him who has discernment, but a rod is for the back of him who is void of understanding.

ends.sectionTitle: Suffering for Doing Good; Shepherds of the Flock
ends.excerpt: And above all things be earnest in your love among yourselves, for love covers a multitude of sins.

connections.label: Subjected to vanity
connections.explanation: Romans 8:20 echoes Ecclesiastes 1:2: Paul says creation was subjected to vanity, not willingly, but in hope of being freed into the glory of God's children. The Preacher opens and closes his book with vanity of vanities; the Greek of both uses the same word.

ends.excerpt: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.” What does man gain from all his labor in which he labors under the sun?
For the creation was subjected to vanity, not of its own will, but because of him who subjected it, in hope

connections.label: From Judah to David
connections.explanation: 1 Chronicles 2:1–15 and Matthew 1:2–6 both tell the line from Judah through Perez, Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmon, Boaz, Obed and Jesse to David. Matthew follows the list and names Rahab and Ruth among the mothers, beside Tamar, whom Chronicles also names. Chronicles places it among the sons of Israel at the head of its history.

ends.sectionTitle: The Line of Judah and of David
ends.excerpt: These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

ends.sectionTitle: The Genealogy and Birth of Jesus
ends.excerpt: Abraham became the father of Isaac. Isaac became the father of Jacob. Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers.

connections.label: The blood of Zechariah
connections.explanation: Matthew 23:35 recalls 2 Chronicles 24:20–22: Jesus warns that all the righteous blood shed on earth will come on his generation, from Abel to Zechariah, killed between the sanctuary and the altar. Chronicles tells of Zechariah son of Jehoiada stoned in the court of the LORD's house; Matthew calls him son of Barachiah, the name of the prophet Zechariah's father.

ends.excerpt: The Spirit of God came on Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest; and he stood above the people, and said to them, “God says, ‘Why do you disobey the LORD’s commandments, so that you can’t prosper?…

ends.sectionTitle: Woes on the Scribes and Pharisees
ends.excerpt: that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the sanctuary and the altar.

connections.label: The radiance of his glory
connections.explanation: Hebrews 1:3 echoes Wisdom 7:26: Hebrews calls the Son the radiance of God's glory and the exact image of his being. Wisdom calls wisdom a reflection of everlasting light, a spotless mirror of God's working and an image of his goodness, words close to Hebrews in Greek.

ends.excerpt: For she is a reflection of everlasting light, an unspotted mirror of the working of God, and an image of his goodness.

ends.sectionTitle: The Son above the Angels and Moses; the Promised Rest
ends.excerpt: His Son is the radiance of his glory, the very image of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power, who, when he had by himself purified us of our sins, sat down on the right…

connections.label: If he is God's son, let God deliver him
connections.explanation: Matthew 27:43 echoes Wisdom 2:17–18: at the cross the chief priests mock Jesus, saying he trusted in God, so let God deliver him now, since he said he was God's Son. In Wisdom the ungodly plot against the righteous man, saying if he is God's son, God will help him and deliver him from his enemies.

ends.sectionTitle: Love Justice; the Reasoning of the Ungodly
ends.excerpt: Let’s see if his words are true. Let’s test what will happen at the end of his life. For if the righteous man is God’s son, he will uphold him, and he will deliver him out of the hand of his…
He trusts in God. Let God deliver him now, if he wants him; for he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”

connections.label: Known from the things that are made
connections.explanation: Romans 1:20–23 echoes Wisdom 13:1–5: Paul says God's invisible power is seen through the things he made, so those who exchanged his glory for images are without excuse. Wisdom says those who did not know the maker from the greatness and beauty of creation were foolish by nature, and partly to blame.

ends.excerpt: For truly all men who had no perception of God were foolish by nature, and didn’t gain power to know him who exists from the good things that are seen. They didn’t recognize the architect from his…

ends.sectionTitle: The Gospel; All under Sin; Righteousness through Faith
ends.excerpt: For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity, that they may be without…

connections.label: Forgive, and you will be forgiven
connections.explanation: Matthew 6:12–14 echoes Sirach 28:2: in the Lord's Prayer the disciples ask to be forgiven as they forgive, and Jesus adds that the Father forgives those who forgive others. Ben Sira ties the pardon of one's own sins in prayer to forgiving a neighbour's wrong first.

ends.excerpt: Forgive your neighbor the hurt that he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.

ends.sectionTitle: The Sermon on the Mount: Prayer and Trust
ends.excerpt: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors. Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’

connections.label: Swift to hear
connections.explanation: James 1:19 echoes Sirach 5:11: James tells every believer to be swift to hear, slow to speak and slow to anger. Ben Sira says be swift to hear and answer with patience.

ends.excerpt: Be swift to hear and answer with patience. If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; but if not, put your hand over your mouth.

ends.sectionTitle: Trials; Hearing and Doing; Faith and Works
ends.excerpt: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;

connections.label: The yoke and rest
connections.explanation: Matthew 11:28–30 echoes Sirach 51:23–27: Jesus calls the weary to come to him and take his yoke, and find rest for their souls. Ben Sira ends his book calling the untaught to draw near, put their necks under wisdom's yoke, and see how little he laboured to find much rest.

ends.sectionTitle: Simon the High Priest; Ben Sira’s Prayer
ends.excerpt: Draw near to me, all you who are uneducated, and live in the house of instruction. Why therefore are you all lacking in these things, and your souls are very thirsty?
“Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.

connections.label: A better resurrection
connections.explanation: Hebrews 11:35 recalls 2 Maccabees 7:9–14: among the heroes of faith Hebrews names those who were tortured and refused release, so as to gain a better resurrection. Second Maccabees tells of the seven brothers who died under torture for God's laws, the second saying the King of the world will raise them to everlasting life.

ends.sectionTitle: The Seven Brothers and Their Mother
ends.excerpt: When he was at the last gasp, he said, “You, miscreant, release us out of this present life, but the King of the world will raise us who have died for his laws up to an everlasting renewal of life.”
Women received their dead by resurrection. Others were tortured, not accepting their deliverance, that they might obtain a better resurrection.

connections.label: The breath of his mouth
connections.explanation: 2 Thessalonians 2:8 echoes Isaiah 11:4: the lawless one will be revealed, and the Lord will slay him with the breath of his mouth and the brightness of his coming. Isaiah says the shoot of Jesse will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth and kill the wicked with the breath of his lips.

ends.sectionTitle: Assyria Judged; the Shoot from Jesse
ends.excerpt: but he will judge the poor with righteousness, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the…

ends.sectionTitle: Endurance; the Day of the Lord; Idleness
ends.excerpt: Then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord will kill with the breath of his mouth and destroy by the manifestation of his coming;

connections.label: Redeemed from all iniquity
connections.explanation: Titus 2:14 echoes Psalms 130:8: Titus says Christ gave himself to redeem us from all iniquity and purify a people of his own, zealous for good works. The psalm ends its cry from the depths with the hope that the LORD will redeem Israel from all their sins.

ends.excerpt: He will redeem Israel from all their sins.
who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself a people for his own possession, zealous for good works.
